sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, and risk generally increases as utilization rises.
Risk climbs most sharply once utilization passes about 0.72 of the credit limit.
The number of past delinquencies is the second or third most important driver, and risk rises once an applicant has at least one delinquency.
Annual income is also second or third in importance, and higher income is associated with lower predicted risk.
Length of credit history has at most a weak effect, with longer histories associated with somewhat lower risk.
The debt-to-income ratio hardly matters: the data do not show a detectable effect of it on predicted default.
The effect of utilization does not appear to change with the number of delinquencies, and the data do not settle whether the effect of utilization grows with credit history length.
The remaining features, including age, the two standardised application attributes and recent credit inquiries, have negligible influence on the model's predictions.
